about: Phrases a synthetic voice MAY say although they contain Quranic words. Reviewed by islamic-content-scholar; every entry cites its ruling. Used by scripts/verify-no-recitation.py, which masks these phrases before matching. Do not add an entry without a ruling reference. 'units' (optional) limits an entry to the listed units. 'except_units' (optional) excludes the listed units. 'transcripts_only': true applies an entry only to Whisper transcripts (--transcripts). A run is excused only when ONE entry covers it; adjacent entries never combine (Round 4, 3).

phrases.ruling: Part 2, rule 2 (بسم الله, dhikr and Sunnah formulas). Round 4, 3: not for Al-Fatiha verses 1 and 3, where this phrase is the whole ayah (1:1, 1:3)
Part 2, rule 2 and D (the isti'adha is dhikr, not an ayah; 16:98 uses فاستعذ)

phrases.kind: isti'adha (as Whisper spells it in transcripts: ذ heard as د)
phrases.ruling: Part 2, D (the isti'adha; An-Nas 5 explanation); Round 4, 3: APPROVED for Whisper transcripts only. Enforced: honoured only under --transcripts; in a script or page this spelling is a typo and is checked like any other text.
Part 2, A: «واحد لا إله إلا هو» (Ikhlas 1) is the tawhid formula and is allowed; rule 2 (لا إله إلا الله)
Part 2, rule 2 (Names and Attributes of Allah)

Part 2, rule 2 (Names of Allah; forbidden only when presented as the ayah, e.g. as a verse's meaning line, which the AR verse suppression covers). Round 4, 3: not for Al-Fatiha verses 1 and 3, where this phrase is the whole ayah (1:1, 1:3)
Part 2, D (Yusuf AR slide 0: ordinary narrative nouns in the narrator's sentence)
Part 2, C and D (Adam EN 7: dhikr formula, may be voiced in both languages)
Part 2, D (isti'adha; An-Nas 5 explanation named there)
Round 4, 3 (APPROVED: the Sunnah reply to the salam, a greeting and not an ayah; game 04 reply option)

onscreen_only.why: START label: only set as innerHTML of the start stone; never passed to say() or speakText(). The phrase is also approved narrative nouns (Part 2, D).

SURAHS[].ayah: shown in

in the recall card; the card's spoken text is r.speak = recall + ask only.
SURAHS[].ayat[].ar: shown inside <span class=quran>; speak() strips span.quran and «...» before speaking; the ayah fallback no longer speaks at all.
AYAT[].ar: set as textContent of #ayah and #fullSurah only; speech reads exAr/exEn, find text and prompts.

SRC[].ar: shown in

in the 'where from' panel; speak() is only given t(key) game strings.
item name: shown on cards and lists only; speech reads clue and hint only. Approved narrative nouns (Part 2, D).
item name (the fig and the olive, ordinary nouns; 95:1 is «والتين والزيتون»): shown on cards and lists only; speech reads clue and hint only.

about_onscreen_only: String literals in files that use speech synthesis which hold Quranic text but are only ever put on screen. 'field' entries skip a literal under that object key only when the literal is scripture and nothing else; 'text' entries skip a literal containing that exact text. Each says where it is used and why no speech path reaches it. The speak(...) argument rule in the check keeps ayah fields out of speech calls; an entry that stops matching fails the check.
